# DTS89 v4.1 -- apparent polygon tears in GarageGames ZombiePack

## Identified and reproduced

The v4.0 reference rasterizer always supplied a projected object size of
64 pixels to `dts89_runtime_select_detail_from_pixel_size()`. Its actual
orthographic viewport is 460x460, with approximately 206 pixels per model
world unit. `Zombie_02` and `Zombie_03` stand more than 300 pixels high;
therefore the constant of 64 is inappropriate.

- `Zombie_02` at projected size 64: **detail level 3** (coarsest),
  approximately 930 triangles with nonzero screen area during the v4.0 render.
  A conspicuous dark triangular intrusion appears at the shirt/waist seam.
- The same DTS at projected size about 379: **detail level 0**,
  approximately 6535 rasterizable triangles in the current test and the
  waist intrusion disappears.
- Both tests use the same unchanged DTS, skeleton, weight arrays, DDS,
  UV, material binder and CPU skinning implementation.

We located the spike contributing to the dark intrusion directly in the
low-detail pants mesh of `Zombie_02`: mesh 7, triangle 106 references
vertex IDs 174,139,140. The source `skin_initial_verts_bits` gives vertex
174 a significantly higher Z coordinate than the other two. Those indices
and that position are *present in the stored low-detail mesh*. It is not a
malformed index generated by the triangle builder. This does not prove
whether the low-detail artist asset has a defect or simply expects to be
viewed from farther away.

## Fix

New reusable module:

- `include/dts89_lod41.h`
- `src/dts89_lod41.c`

`dts89_lod41_orthographic_axis()` obtains bounds through the existing fixed-
point codec, computes projected screen extent with caller-provided Q16.16
pixels/world-unit and selects the appropriate detail. The current renderer
uses up-axis Z and camera scale 206 pixels/world-unit.

This is specifically an **orthographic camera helper**. Perspective
projection should use projected radius and distance/FOV, not this function.
The module never assumes that closest LOD is universally required: far-away
models must still be able to select their lower detail versions.

## Reproducible tests

Build:

    make CFLAGS='-std=c89 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic-errors -Iinclude'

Run:

    ./tools/dts89_lod41_selftest
    ./tools/dts89_pose37_selftest
    ./tools/dts89_lighting40_selftest

Test corpus render command:

    ./tools/dts89_lit40_render model.dts materials.cs dds_dir out.ppm

The last command now computes detail automatically, instead of always
asking for 64 pixels. On the supplied six ZombiePack 1.1 DTS, projected
size was about 379 pixels and the selected level was 0. The four sampled
poses of `Zombie` Attack1 also selected level 0.

## What remains unproven

- A perfect vertex-for-vertex comparison with the original Torque GFX path.
- Whether every seam in every lower-quality LOD of the source assets is
  intentional or a low-LOD modeling imperfection.
- Sorted translucency, full alpha blending and advanced material passes.
- Full perspective clipping and subpixel top-left fill conventions of the
  Torque GFX backend. The current CPU rasterizer remains a reference tool.

No geometry, DTS contents, skinning weights, UVs or materials were altered
as part of this correction.
